I personally don't use TikTok, but from my secondhand observations, the platform seems to have turned into a giant treasure trove of dubious advice. Recently, a video suggested that if your iPhone overheats, you should put it in the freezer……

Engadget only cited one example.

This is obviously something you shouldn't do. Doing so will very likely cause moisture to condense on the phone's internal components, whether during the time it's in the freezer or after you take it out. Thermal shock is also a potential issue, particularly since lithium batteries are especially sensitive to such conditions.

The UK has been experiencing a heatwave over the past few weeks (by British standards), and mobile phone repair shops reportedly saw a noticeable increase in cases of people bricking their devices after following this advice.

If your iPhone really does overheat, Apple's official recommendation is to move it to a cooler environment and let it cool down naturally. However, don't leave it in the car. On hot days, even the glove compartment inside a car can get hot enough to cause damage, or even start a battery fire.
